title: Daemon treats a task as merged when its branch is an ancestor of the goal branch (fix rounds)
spec:
Why: merge(fix_round) sets merged_into only on the fix-round task; the original stays status done with merged_into unset. Inside an open goal the daemon's gate stage would then re-gate and re-review already-merged work (the first smoke run created T-0057..T-0062 this way; T-0063's closed-goal guard covers closed goals only). Depends on T-0063 merged into goal/T-0043.

What (2 files: orchestrator/daemon.py, tests/test_daemon.py; worktree off goal/T-0043):
1. daemon.py: `def already_merged(t) -> bool`: if t has merged_into → True; else if t has a parent and the branch `task/<id>` exists and `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<id> goal/<parent>` (run from ROOT, check=False) returns 0 → set `bus.update(t["id"], merged_into=f"goal/{parent}", merged_via="ancestor")` and return True; else False. Call it at the top of the gate stage (and anywhere else a done execute task is considered un-merged), before any stamp is claimed. Never raise if git is unavailable or the branches are missing (treat as not merged).
2. tests/test_daemon.py: with a scratch repo from the harness: create goal/G, a task branch with one commit, fast-forward goal/G to it; a done execute task for that branch with merged_into unset → one tick sets merged_into=goal/G, merged_via=ancestor, and neither the gate nor review is triggered (monkeypatched subprocess.run for tests-green and spawn.run_worker not called). A second task whose branch is NOT an ancestor is gated as before.

Run `uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests`. Commit: "daemon: mark ancestor-merged tasks as merged before gating (fix rounds)" with a revert-path body.
acceptance: uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests exits 0 with the new ancestor test
a done execute task whose task/<id> branch is an ancestor of goal/<parent> gets merged_into set and is never gated or reviewed
a non-ancestor done task is still gated
git diff --stat limited to orchestrator/daemon.py and tests/test_daemon.py

result.summary:
Committed on `task/T-0064` at `901306a`.

## Summary

Added `already_merged(t)` to `orchestrator/daemon.py`: returns `True` if `merged_into` is already set, or if `task/<id>` exists and is a git ancestor of `goal/<parent>` — in which case it stamps `merged_into`/`merged_via=ancestor` on the spot. Wired it into `gate()` (replacing the bare `t.get("merged_into")` check) and `merge_reviewed()` (replacing `src.get("merged_into")`), both before any pipeline stamp is claimed. Never raises — a missing branch or git binary is just treated as "not merged".

While writing the test I hit a real gotcha in the existing harness: `gate_green()` faked `daemon.subprocess.run` unconditionally for *any* args, but `daemon.subprocess` is the literal stdlib `subprocess` module, shared with `spawn.git()`. Once `already_merged()` started making real git calls through that same channel, the old blanket fake made every git check silently report success. Fixed `gate_green()` to only fake tests-green/osascript calls and pass everything else (git) through to the real `subprocess.run`.

Files changed: `orchestrator/daemon.py`, `tests/test_daemon.py`.

Test output (final run): `Ran 87 tests in 10.379s / OK` — no failures. `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh` also exits 0.

Nothing left outstanding on this task.
result.review: other account, different model; label PR same-family-review
